security_audit.summary: Most static external command findings are false positives from Markdown fences and inline commit examples. The Bash hook on SKILL.md line 9 is confirmed because it runs automatically and appends to a hidden home-directory log.

remediation.issue: Hidden Bash hook writes to the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the PostToolUse hook or require clear opt-in before writing logs. Prefer a visible project-local log if logging is required.

remediation.issue: The Bash hook matcher is broad for a commit-message helper.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow any hook to explicit Git diff review workflows, or remove automatic hooks from the marketplace package.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes mutating Git examples such as commit and amend.
remediation.suggestion: Label mutating commands as user-run examples and require explicit confirmation before suggesting execution.

content.value_statement: Vague commits make reviews and release notes harder. This skill analyzes staged Git changes and drafts structured Conventional Commit messages.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged Git diff output to identify the main change.
Suggests Conventional Commit types, scopes, summaries, and bodies.
Provides examples for feature, fix, refactor, and breaking change commits.
Guides selective staging, amending, and review workflows with Git commands.
Checks commit message quality against length and style guidelines.
limitations: Requires staged changes or diff text for the best result.
Does not validate issue numbers or project-specific release policies automatically.
May suggest Git commands that modify repository history when the user asks.
The included hook writes a local hidden log unless removed.

use_cases.title: Daily Feature Work
use_cases.description: Turn staged feature changes into a concise commit summary and explanatory body.

use_cases.title: Review Cleanup
use_cases.description: Split noisy staged changes into clearer commit types and scopes before review.

use_cases.title: Release Preparation
use_cases.description: Mark breaking changes and write commit bodies that support changelog generation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft A Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commit message with a short body.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Type And Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these staged changes and choose the best commit type and scope before drafting the message.

prompt_templates.title: Split Logical Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Help split my staged diff into atomic commits and write messages for each logical change.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this staged diff for breaking changes, issue references, and release-note wording before writing the final commit message.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add password reset email flow and tests.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(auth): add password reset email flow. Body: Explain the new email flow and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Staged changes fix a crash when profile data is missing.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: fix(profile): handle missing user data. Body: Add null checks and cover the empty-state path.

output_examples.input: Staged changes update API response format and client parsing.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(api)!: standardize response format. Body: Include a breaking change note for clients.

best_practices: Stage one logical change before asking for a commit message.
Review the proposed type, scope, and summary before committing.
Add context about issue numbers, breaking changes, and user impact.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to commit, amend, or stage files without reviewing the command first.
Do not combine unrelated changes into one generated message.
Do not paste secrets or private diffs into shared conversations.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You should confirm any Git command before it runs.

faq.question: What commit style does it use?
faq.answer: It focuses on Conventional Commits with type, optional scope, summary, body, and breaking change notes.

faq.question: Does it need staged changes?
faq.answer: Staged changes produce the most accurate result, but pasted diff summaries can also work.

faq.question: Can it help split large commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify logical groups and suggest separate messages for each group.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review generated messages, mutating Git commands, and any local logging behavior before installation.
